name: Juan de Castro
summary:
Juan de Castro (1431–1506) was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal. He served as the Bishop of Burgos from 1479 to 1485, where he implemented various reforms aimed at improving the lives of the local population. During his tenure, he also played a crucial role in the Spanish Inquisition, serving as an advisor to King Ferdinand II of Aragon. His efforts led to the establishment of new laws and regulations that had significant consequences for the region.

As a cardinal, Juan de Castro participated in several high-level diplomatic meetings, including the Council of Florence, where he represented the interests of Spain. He also played a key role in the papacy's dealings with various European monarchs, including King John II of Portugal.

Juan de Castro's legacy can be seen in the numerous reforms and laws that were implemented during his time as Bishop of Burgos. His efforts had a lasting impact on the region, shaping its social, political, and religious landscape for centuries to come.

The sheer scale of Juan de Castro's contributions is reflected in the fact that he was appointed as a cardinal at the age of 35, making him one of the youngest cardinals in history.
